title: Group Dynamics: Group Behaviour & Leadership
summary: Group dynamics: group behaviour, group decision-making, group polarization, groupthink (Janis), social facilitation, social loafing and leadership styles.
objectives: Describe group dynamics and group behaviour.
Distinguish social facilitation from social loafing.
revision: Group dynamics: group behaviour, groupthink (Janis), social facilitation, social loafing, leadership styles.
traps: Social facilitation = better (simple tasks); social loafing = less effort (groups).

notes.t: Two or more people who interact, influence one another and share a common goal.
Irving Janis's term for a mode of thinking where the desire for unanimity overrides realistic appraisal of alternatives, leading to poor decisions.
Group polarization: group discussion strengthens members' initial tendencies, shifting decisions toward extremes.
Improved performance on simple or well-learned tasks in the presence of others.
Reduced individual effort when working in a group compared with working alone.

i: Democratic: leader involves group in decisions

notes.t: UGC NET frequently asks about groupthink, social facilitation, social loafing and leadership styles.

mnemonics.title: GSL
mnemonics.text: G — Groupthink (Janis, unanimity over appraisal), S — Social facilitation/loafing, L — Leadership styles (authoritarian/democratic/laissez-faire)

flashcards.a: Desire for unanimity overrides realistic appraisal → poor decisions.
Better performance on simple tasks in presence of others.
Reduced effort in a group vs alone.
